deep.reconstruction:
The page has no mathematics: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is part of Riemann's natural-philosophical and psychological drafts on 'Geistesmassen'. It continues the numbered theses of the previous page (Blatt 13) and then gives a cleaner redraft headed 'Blatt 14'.

(A) Thesis 12 is the conclusion of theses 10 and 11 on the previous page. Thesis 10 says each Geistesmasse strives to produce an equally formed one, and so strives to restore the motion-form of matter at which it was formed. Thesis 11 says this striving acts wherever there is a connection, weaker the more remote the connection. Hence (12): the motion-form of matter at a given place is fixed at each instant by two things.
(1) All Geistesmassen connected with the Geistesmasse formed there immediately before. Each counts according to the degree of its connection, and each strives to restore the motion-form at which it was formed.
(2) The external forces, which depend on the position of the matter.
A purely interpretive modern gloss (mine, not Riemann's): write the local motion-form as a state x. The rule then reads like a superposition: dx/dt = sum_i w_i * (attraction of x toward the pattern x_i at which mass i was formed) + F_ext(position). Here w_i decreases with the remoteness of the connection to the most recently formed mass. This loosely resembles associative-memory or attractor dynamics. Riemann writes no equation.

(B) 'Blatt 14' (Reproduction by memory and imagination) is a fair-copy version of theses 1–4.
- With every simple act of thought something lasting and substantial enters the soul. It appears to us as a unity but, as the expression of something extended in space and time, seems to contain an inner manifold. Hence the name 'Geistesmasse'. All thinking is the formation of new Geistesmassen.
- Their entry into the soul causes our ideas (Vorstellungen); their differing inner state causes the quality of those ideas.
- New Geistesmassen fuse, combine or 'complicate' with one another and with older ones, each to a definite degree. These are Herbart's terms Verschmelzung and Complication. The conditions governing the kind and strength of these connections were, Riemann says, found only partly by Herbart; he will supplement and modify them. The connections rest chiefly on the inner affinity (Verwandtschaft) of the masses.
- The soul is a compact, most intimately and manifoldly interconnected Geistesmasse. It grows constantly through entering masses, and its development (Fortbildung) rests on this.

Margin: '2.' (ordering) and '+) cf. ob[en] S. 18'. This most likely cross-references p. 18, i.e. the note on the previous page about matter (Stoff) streaming into ponderable atoms.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible; the page contains no computation.

Conceptually, thesis 12 is asserted as following ('daher') from theses 10–11. It does so only if one also assumes that the strivings of different Geistesmassen combine additively or according to degree of connection, and together with external forces. This superposition assumption is implicit.

results.what: Thesis 12: the local motion-form of matter is determined by the strivings of all connected Geistesmassen, weighted by degree of connection, plus external position-dependent forces.
results.modern_name: Speculative psychophysical (associationist) dynamics; loosely analogous to associative-memory / attractor models.
results.usually_credited_to: Associationist psychology (Herbart 1824–25, Fechner 1860 for psychophysics); attractor memory models much later (Hopfield 1982), only as a loose analogy.

results.what: Doctrine of 'Geistesmassen': lasting substantial traces of each act of thought; their fusion and complication with older masses; the soul as a growing compact Geistesmasse.
results.modern_name: Herbartian psychology of ideas (Verschmelzung/Komplikation); memory-trace (engram) theory.
results.usually_credited_to: J. F. Herbart (Psychologie als Wissenschaft, 1824–25); Riemann's version is published in his Werke (1876) under 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik'.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's well-known philosophical fragments on Geistesmassen. They were published by Dedekind and Weber in the Gesammelte Werke (1876) and are discussed in the Riemann literature. The page contains no mathematics and nothing beyond the known text.
transcription_corrections: Margin note '+) cf. Oken[?] S. 18' is more plausibly '+) cf. oben S. 18' ('see above, p. 18'). It cross-references the note marked '(S. 18)' on the previous page about matter entering ponderable atoms; a reference to Oken is unlikely.
In Blatt 14 the image reads roughly 'aufs Engste' / 'aufs engste'; the capitalisation is uncertain but the sense is unchanged.
Thesis 12 item 1 reads 'mit der dort unmittelbar vorher gebildeten Geistesmasse zusammenhängenden Geistesmassen'; the machine transcription agrees with the image.
